neighbours.label: the first split piece ' am' or ' en' of a verb of pleasing or surprising an audience (am|aze, am|use, en|l|iven)
fire: Her memory for dates will never cease to amaze the whole family.
Puppets were used to amuse the children at the party.
The way he plays chess continues to amaze his teachers.
A few silly jokes helped to enliven the long dinner.
Clowns came out between the acts to amuse the crowd.
Those old stories still amaze anyone who hears them.
Fresh colors will enliven even the dullest room.
He tried hard to amuse his sister during the drive.
quiet: Her memory for dates will never cease to help the whole family.
Puppets were used to teach the children at the party.
The way he plays chess continues to worry his teachers.
A few silly jokes helped to shorten the long dinner.
Clowns came out between the acts to greet the crowd.
Those old stories still reach anyone who hears them.
Fresh colors will brighten even the dullest room.
He tried hard to calm his sister during the drive.

notes: Card: ' am' x7, ' has' x3, ' en', ' frequently', with amaze, amply, amuse and enlivened at the top. Probes: ' am' in amaze 0.910, ' en' in enlivened 0.551, ' am' in amuse 0.487, ' am' in amply 0.306; 'bother' 0.154, 'defied' 0.120. Tokens are checked for every fire sentence; forms that are whole tokens (amazed, amused) are not in the test. Near misses use other verbs in the same frames.
